niche: connected TV and streaming advertising agency
prompt_text: What is the best connected TV advertising agency?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t one “best” connected-TV (CTV) advertising agency — the right partner depends on your goals, budget, target audiences, measurement needs and whether you want a full-service media agency or a specialist programmatic/platform partner.

How to choose the best agency for you
- Define goals: brand awareness, reach, lead generation/DR, foot traffic or sales attribution?  
- Scale & geography: global vs regional vs single U.S. market.  
- Buying approach: direct platform buys (Roku/Hulu, publishers) vs programmatic across CTV inventory.  
- Data/identity needs: do you need audience targeting using your CRM/1st-party data?  
- Creative & tech stack: do you have CTV-ready video assets and do you need dynamic/ad creative services?  
- Measurement & attribution: incremental reach, ad-effectiveness, conversions, ROAS — which vendors do you require?  
- Budget & timeline: minimum spend and campaign duration.

Agency types and when to pick them
- Global/full-service media agencies (best if you need scale, cross-channel planning, and holding-company relationships): WPP/GroupM (Wavemaker, Mindshare), Omnicom (OMD, PHD), Publicis (Starcom, Zenith), Dentsu (Carat, iProspect), IPG (Initiative, UM).  
- Programmatic/tech-forward specialists (best for data-driven targeting and programmatic CTV buys): agencies that work closely with DSPs like The Trade Desk or DV360, or boutique programmatic shops.  
- Platform/direct partners (best for guaranteed inventory and publisher/streamer relationships): Roku Advertising, Hulu/Disney, Amazon DSP, Samsung Ads, Pluto/Tubi. Often you can buy directly or via agency trading desks.  
- CTV-focused independent agencies (best for nimble strategy, creative and bespoke CTV expertise): look for boutique shops with proven CTV case studies and measurement partners (name selection varies by market).

Vendors & tech you’ll commonly see (helps evaluate agency capabilities)
- DSPs/platforms: The Trade Desk, DV360, Amazon DSP, proprietary platforms from Roku/Hulu.  
- Measurement & verification: Innovid, Samba TV, iSpot, Nielsen (streaming measurement), IAS/DoubleVerify.  
- Creative & dynamic ad tools: Innovid, Jivox, Celtra.  
- Data activation: LiveRamp, Oracle, Salesforce integrations.

Practical shortlist (by capability)
- If you want global reach and cross-channel integration: a major media agency from WPP, Omnicom, Publicis, Dentsu or IPG.  
- If you want programmatic expertise and first-party-data activation: an agency with strong Trade Desk or DV360 experience (or a programmatic specialist).  
- If you want direct publisher/streaming relationships and guaranteed CTV inventory: work through Roku Advertising, Hulu/Disney, Amazon DSP or specialty teams within large agencies that have direct buys.

How to evaluate agencies (questions to ask)
- Which CTV inventory partners do you buy from (Roku, Hulu, publisher apps, programmatic exchanges)?  
- How do you target audiences and activate my first‑party/CRM data?  
- Which DSPs, measurement vendors and verification partners do you use?  
- Can you show CTV case studies with results similar to our goals?  
- What are your minimum media spend requirements, fees and reporting cadence?  
- How do you handle creative (repurposing assets, dynamic creatives, QA/testing)?  
- How do you measure incremental reach vs linear TV and attribution of conversions?

If you tell me: campaign goals, budget, geography, audience and whether you need creative/measurement help, I can recommend a short list of specific agencies or platform partners that match your needs. Which of those details can you share?
